name: compose-docker-socket-mount
task_triggers: adding a volume to a service
mounting the docker socket into a container
attack_scenario: A compromised app with docker.sock mounted runs 'docker run -v /:/host --privileged' to mount and write the host filesystem, adding a root SSH key or cron job to take over the host.
negative_test_hint: from inside the container run "docker run -v /:/host --privileged alpine" and assert it fails because the Docker socket is not mounted

exemplar.explanation: The Docker daemon socket is root-equivalent on the host: anything with access to it can create privileged containers, bind-mount the host root, and read every other container's secrets. Read-only (:ro) does not help because the API still allows container creation, so the socket must never be mounted into an application container.
